newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat prices steady on E.Europe sales.
newsitem.headline: German wheat prices steady on E.Europe sales.

text.p: German wheat sellers kept prices steady this week after recent bread wheat sales to Poland and Uzbekistan, brokers said on Wednesday.
But southern and western Europe were not absorbing German wheat and future eastern European business was unclear.
"The French sell their wheat in the Benelux countries and Britain...Southern Europe has bought some wheat overseas for blending," one said.
"There seems to be little room for German supplies at these prices in the east...domestic millers are also refusing to get involved in negotiations."
Feed wheat prices remained stable as the strenth of sterling deterred buyers from taking up the British supplies that were offered.
British feed wheat cif North Germany was offered at 275 marks.
But farmers shrugged off a lack of consumer interest and continued to withhold grain in the hope of higher prices next year.
The Hamburg grain exchange this week reduced its new crop bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 hagberg) by 2.50 marks to 285 and maintained its spot feed wheat price free Hamburg at 275.
In the fob export market, 12 percent material was quoted around 295 marks, 13 percent wheat was at 297-302 and top qualities with 14 percent up to 318 marks.
The price floor of fob barley was raised five marks from a 250-270 marks range last week, reflecting costs of holding the grain since the harvest.
Domestic barley free delivered Hamburg was offered unchanged at 257.50 marks a tonne, with 255 paid.
Fob bread rye was quoted at 262.50 marks and feed rye at 255-262.
The November intervention price for all grains will be 230.50 marks when the buying season begins.
